clue.text: Editor likes to have this italic typo corrected

indicators.note: a typo that is corrected has its letters put right, so the words italic and typo are rearranged

explanation.surface: An editor fusses over a misprint in italic type that needs fixing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrected' rearranges ITALIC and TYPO together; the definition is a description, the quality of being current that editors prize in news.
explanation.definitionFit: Editors want stories that are current and relevant to the day, which is what topicality means.

clue.text: Name American river flowing to Atlantic

parts.note: to tag something is to name or label it

explanation.surface: Naming an American river that runs to the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tagus flows across Spain and Portugal and reaches the Atlantic at Lisbon.

clue.text: Alarm about old sign pointing in all directions

indicators.note: one word placed about others goes around them, so the alarm word encloses the rest

parts.note: panic is a state of alarm
the Ram (Aries) is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: An alarm goes off near an ancient signpost whose arms point every way.
explanation.definitionFit: A panoramic view takes in every direction around the viewer, a wide sweeping outlook.

clue.text: Contrasting incentives to combine another vegetable with celery

parts.note: a carrot is a vegetable other than celery
and means together with
celery comes in sticks, so a stick stands for celery

explanation.surface: A recipe suggestion to mix a second vegetable in with some celery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to combine' is only a link; the pieces simply sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a reward offered alongside a threatened punishment, two opposite ways of motivating.

clue.text: A match for leader of rebellion

definitions.meaning: an old name for a friction match struck to light a fire
Satan, who led the angels' revolt against heaven

explanation.surface: Someone equal to the person heading an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is both an old word for a match and Satan, leader of the rebel angels.

clue.text: Confronted change of policy and took charge

parts.note: a tack is a course of action, and changing tack is changing policy
led means was in charge of or headed

explanation.surface: A leader faced a policy reversal and assumed command.
explanation.definitionFit: To tackle a problem or person is to face up to and deal with them.

clue.text: Accommodation for one or more in uniform

definitions.meaning: a set of rooms on one floor where a single person or several may live
... as in a ... rate, the same throughout

explanation.surface: Living quarters for a person or group dressed in regulation clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat is an apartment, and flat also means even and unvarying, as in a flat fee.

clue.text: Artist using blue, red, and yellow primarily

parts.note: feeling blue is feeling low

indicators.note: the leading letters of these colour words are picked out, as primarily means first of all

explanation.surface: A painter working with the three primary colours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' takes the first letters of both 'red' and 'yellow'. L. S. Lowry was an English painter of northern industrial scenes.
explanation.definitionFit: L. S. Lowry was an English painter famous for matchstick figures in industrial towns.

clue.text: Guernsey, for example, is so closely integrated

definitions.meaning: a guernsey is a thick fisherman's jumper made with dense close stitching
describes a community bound together by strong ties

explanation.surface: The Channel Island of Guernsey is described as a close community.
explanation.walkthrough: Guernsey looks like the Channel Island, but here it is the woollen sweater (jumper) named after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes both densely knitted wool and a community whose members are closely bound.

clue.text: Traitor's constitutional right not to talk with pressman

parts.note: the Fifth Amendment of the US Constitution protects against self-incrimination
a columnist is a newspaper writer

explanation.surface: A traitor pleads the right to silence alongside a journalist.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Traitor's' stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a fifth column is a secret sympathiser working against their own country, a traitor.

clue.text: Referring to whole class, or boy with limited intelligence

parts.note: gen is slang for information, a scrap of intelligence
Eric is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A remark about a whole class, or about one slow-witted lad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limited intelligence' looks like an insult to the boy, but it is GEN, British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: Generic describes something applying to a whole group or category rather than one member.

clue.text: Talk in Eastern country about West? Good

indicators.note: the country word goes about the next piece, wrapping round it

parts.note: China is a country in the East

explanation.surface: A conversation in an Asian nation about the West: is it positive?
explanation.definitionFit: A chinwag is informal British slang for a chat or gossip.

clue.text: For us, world endlessly in turmoil is sad

indicators.note: letters thrown into turmoil are jumbled into a new order
endlessly means the word world loses its final letter

explanation.surface: For us, a world forever in chaos is a cause of grief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims WORLD to WORL; 'in turmoil' then rearranges FOR, US and WORL.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorrowful means full of grief, which is a synonym for sad.

clue.text: Meeting one included in calendar after experiment

indicators.note: the saint comes after the experiment word in the answer

parts.note: a try is an attempt or experiment
a saint is one included in the church calendar of feast days, abbreviated St

explanation.surface: A meeting slotted into the diary following a trial run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one included in calendar' is a saint, since saints have days in the church calendar; ST is the usual abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A tryst is a romantic meeting or assignation arranged in advance.

clue.text: A bird found on South Pacific island group

indicators.note: the bird pieces are found sitting on top of the abbreviation for South

parts.note: the moa is an extinct flightless bird of New Zealand

explanation.surface: A bird is spotted on a group of islands in the South Pacific.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South' looks like part of 'South Pacific' but gives S; 'found on' places A MOA after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Samoa is an archipelago in the South Pacific Ocean, made up of several islands.

clue.text: Confess and reveal one diamond, perhaps

parts.note: to sing is slang for confessing to the police
to let on is to reveal a secret

explanation.surface: Someone owns up and shows off a solitaire gem.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, a lone card of a suit in a hand is so called; a single diamond held is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games a singleton is the only card held in a suit, such as one lone diamond.

clue.text: Introduce working from nine to five, for example

definitions.text: from nine to five, for example

indicators.note: letters set working are put to use in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Bringing in office hours from nine until five.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from nine to five' reads as office hours, but it is a cut in number from nine down to five.
explanation.definitionFit: Going from nine down to five is a decrease in number, an example of making something smaller.

clue.text: Right in the middle of concert I broke out

indicators.note: the right abbreviation sits in the middle of the following words
the letters broke up, which jumbles them into a new order

explanation.surface: Justice exploded in the middle of a musical performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like part of 'broke out', but it is the definition: a sum that is out is wrong. 'broke' rearranges CONCERT with R put in, CONCRERT, and I stands first.
explanation.definitionFit: Out can mean mistaken or inaccurate, as when a reckoning is out by a few pounds.

clue.text: Trash I consumed as Pharisee

indicators.note: to trash something is to wreck it, so the letters are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: I ate rubbish, like a self-righteous religious figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trash' looks like a noun but is the verb, rearranging I and CONSUMED.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicodemus was a Pharisee in the Gospel of John who visited Jesus by night.

clue.text: Get wrong message from marks I cut

parts.note: M is an abbreviation for the mark, the old German currency
to shear is to cut

explanation.surface: Misunderstand the meaning of the marks I have trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'message from' is a link, saying the hint for the definition comes from what follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To mishear is to catch what is said incorrectly, getting the words wrong.

clue.text: Put extra fat in contract

definitions.meaning: pastry is ... by adding lard or butter, called ...
to make or become smaller in length

explanation.surface: Pad out a written agreement with superfluous material.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to add fat to pastry dough and to make something briefer.

clue.text: Element of publicity that's not banned

indicators.note: an element of a word is a part of it, so the answer is found inside the word

explanation.surface: Part of a publicity campaign that is permitted.
explanation.definitionFit: Licit means lawful or permitted, the opposite of illicit or prohibited.

clue.text: Settle without difficulty

definitions.meaning: to come down and rest on something, as a bird lands on a branch
easy, not demanding, as in work that is not heavy

explanation.surface: Resolve the matter easily.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird may light on a branch, settling there, and easy work is light work.

clue.text: Court's covering for informer

definitions.meaning: the turf surface of a lawn tennis court
British slang for someone who tells the police about criminals

explanation.surface: A tribunal provides protection to someone who tells tales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests a law court, which fits 'informer', but it is a tennis court and its lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawn tennis courts are surfaced with turf, and a police informer is a grass in British slang.

clue.text: Music for the army, perhaps, but not the fleet

definitions.text: Music for the army, perhaps, but not the fleet

parts.words: Music for the army, perhaps, but not the fleet
parts.note: military music played at a stately pace; fleet reads as the navy but means swift, which this music is not

explanation.surface: A military band tune suits soldiers but not sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the fleet' suggests the navy as opposed to the army; it is fleet meaning fast.
explanation.definitionFit: A solemn military piece played at a measured pace for soldiers parading, the opposite of fast.

clue.text: House rent raised for temporary accommodation

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the word goes upwards, read from bottom to top

parts.note: to let a property is to rent it out

explanation.surface: A landlord puts the rent up on a short-term home.
explanation.definitionFit: Guests stay in a hotel for a short time, so it is lodging that is temporary.

clue.text: Issued 100 in the instalment of shares

indicators.note: the issued and hundred pieces are placed in the word the

parts.note: ran means issued or flowed out
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A hundred were issued as part of a share offering.
explanation.definitionFit: A tranche is a portion of a larger sum, especially a block of shares released at one time.

clue.text: Weapon on submarine I had submerged in river

indicators.note: something submerged in a river goes inside it

parts.note: the Trent is a major river in the English Midlands
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: A naval officer recalls a weapon he dropped into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Trent is a major river in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Trident is the ballistic missile carried by British and American submarines.

clue.text: Accommodation for hobby, say, in secluded place

definitions.meaning: a hobby is a small falcon, and a bird lives in this

explanation.surface: Somewhere quiet to house one's pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hobby' looks like a pastime, but it is a small falcon.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird such as a falcon is housed in a nest, and a cosy hideaway is also called one.

clue.text: Final result of accumulating scores of ponies?

definitions.text: Final result of accumulating scores of ponies?

parts.words: Final result of accumulating scores of ponies?
parts.note: a pony is slang for 25 pounds, so forty of them make a thousand pounds, slang a grand; the sum is the last figure reached by adding up

explanation.surface: Tallying up how many horses there are in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a pony is £25 and a grand £1,000, so scores of ponies add up to grands.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the final sum after all subtotals are added together.
